glosses: Weather, especially favourable or fair weather.

glosses: The short term state of the atmosphere at a specific time and place, including the temperature, relative humidity, cloud cover, precipitation, wind, etc.

examples.text: What's the weather like today?
We'll go for a walk when the weather's better.
The garden party was called off due to bad weather.
Here and there, the weather on the sea allowed two of their friends to hear and see, too.
Human beings love to talk about the weather.

glosses: Unpleasant or destructive atmospheric conditions, and their effects.

examples.text: Wooden garden furniture must be well oiled as it is continuously exposed to weather.

glosses: The direction from which the wind is blowing; used attributively to indicate the windward side.

examples.text: One complained of a bad cold in his head, upon which Jonah mixed him a pitch-like potion of gin and molasses, which he swore was a sovereign cure for all colds and catarrhs whatsoever, never mind of how long standing, or whether caught off the coast of Labrador, or on the weather side of an ice-island.

glosses: A situation.
A storm; a tempest.

examples.text: What gusts of weather from that gathering cloud / My thoughts presage!

glosses: To expose to the weather, or show the effects of such exposure, or to withstand such effects.

examples.text: The organisms […] seem indestructible, while the hard matrix in which they are embedded has weathered from around them.
[An eagle] soaring through his wide empire of the air / To weather his broad sails.

glosses: To sustain the trying effect of; to bear up against and overcome; to endure; to resist.

examples.text: "Come hither! come hither! my little daughter, / And do not tremble so; / For I can weather the roughest gale, That ever wind did blow."

April 18, 1850, Frederick William Robertson, An Address Delivered to the Members of the Working Man's Institute

glosses: To break down, of rocks and other materials, under the effects of exposure to rain, sunlight, temperature, and air.

examples.text: Lichens' ability to weather makes them a geological force, yet they do more than disolve the physical features of the world.

glosses: To pass to windward in a vessel, especially to beat 'round.

examples.text: to weather a cape    to weather another ship

glosses: To endure or survive an event or action without undue damage.

examples.text: Joshua weathered a collision with a freighter near South Africa.

glosses: To place (a hawk) unhooded in the open air.
